Surah 71: Nuh

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿Indeed, We sent Nuh﴾. It is said that its meaning in Syriac is "the one who remains" (al-sakin).

﴿That warn﴾: frighten. Its original form is "bi-an andhir" (with "that warn"), so the preposition was dropped and the verb was connected directly to it. Its grammatical position (mahall) is in the genitive according to al-Khalil, and in the accusative according to others. Or "an" is explanatory (mufassira), meaning "i.e." (ay), because sending carries the sense of "saying."

﴿Warn your people before a painful punishment comes to them﴾: the punishment of the Hereafter, or the Flood.

"He said: O my people," he attributed them to himself, to show compassion,

"Indeed I am to you a warner," one who frightens,

"clear," I make clear to you the message of God, in a language you know.

﴿That you worship Allah﴾: make Him one (wahhidu-hu), and "an" here is like "an undhir" (that I warn) in the two cases (i.e., it is the interpretive/explanatory "an" in both readings).

﴿And fear Him﴾: beware of disobeying Him.

﴿And obey me﴾: in what I command you with and what I forbid you from. He attributed it to Himself, because obedience may be due to other than Allah (Exalted is He), unlike worship.

**Commentary of al-Nasafi (*Madarik al-Tanzil*) on Surah 71, verse 4:**

﴿He will forgive you your sins﴾: this is the response (*jawab*) to the imperative.

﴿Your sins﴾: the preposition *min* here is explanatory (*li-l-bayan*), as in His saying: ﴿So shun the abomination of idols﴾ (Surah al-Hajj 22:30). Or it is partitive (*li-l-tab'id*), because what lies between a person and other people is held against him after Islam, such as retribution (*qisas*) and other rights. Thus it is reported in *Sharh al-Ta'wilat*.

﴿And He will defer you to a specified term﴾: this is the time of your death.

﴿Indeed, the term of Allah﴾, that is, death,

﴿when it comes, is not deferred, if only you knew﴾: that is, if only you knew the regret that will befall you at the end of your term, you would have believed.

It is said that God (Exalted is He) had decreed, for example, that if the people of Noah believed, He would let them live a thousand years, and if they did not believe, He would destroy them at the end of nine hundred. So it was said to them: "Believe, and He will defer you to a specified term," meaning you will be granted a thousand years. Then He informed them that the thousand-year term, when it comes, is not deferred, just as this other term is deferred.

It is also said that they feared destruction at the hands of their own people because of their belief and their response to Noah, peace be upon him. So he, peace be upon him, gave them assurance against that, and promised them that by believing they would remain until the term appointed for them, which they would not have reached had they not believed. That is: if you submit, you will remain until a specified term, safe from your enemies.
﴿He said, "My Lord, indeed I have invited my people night and day."﴾ Persistently, without slackening.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 71, verse 6:

﴿But my call only increased them in flight﴾ — away from Your obedience. This increase is attributed to his call because it was the occasion for it in their case, even though the call was not in reality the cause of their fleeing. It is like His saying: ﴿As for those in whose hearts is a disease, it adds filth to their filth﴾ [al-Tawba: 125]. The Qur'an does not in reality cause an increase in filth. And a man would take his son to Nuh, peace be upon him, and say: "Beware of this one, and do not let him deceive you, for my father has enjoined me concerning him."

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 71, verse 7:

﴿And indeed, every time I have called them﴾, to faith in You,

﴿so that You might forgive them﴾, meaning: so that they would believe and You would forgive them. He suffices with mention of the effect (al-musabbab) and omits the cause (al-sabab).

﴿they put their fingers in their ears﴾, they stopped up their hearing so that they would not hear my words,

﴿and covered themselves with their garments﴾, and wrapped themselves in their clothing, so that they would not see me, out of aversion to looking at the face of one who advises them in the religion of Allah,

﴿and persisted﴾, and remained upon their disbelief,

﴿and were arrogant with great arrogance﴾, and magnified themselves against responding to me. The mention of the verbal noun (masdar) is evidence of the extreme degree of their arrogance.

Verse 8 of Surah 71 (Nuh): "Then I called to them openly."

"Jihaaran" (openly) is a verbal noun (maṣdar) in the position of a circumstantial qualifier (ḥāl), meaning "publicly declaring" (mujāhiran). Alternatively, it is a verbal noun of "da'awtuhum" (I called them), like "qa'ada al-qurfusā'" (he sat in the crouching manner), because jihār is one of the two types of calling (du'ā'); that is, "I made the call manifest to them in assemblies."

Then indeed I called out to them openly, and I spoke to them in private, a private speaking.

That is, I mixed my calling to them openly with calling them in secret. The sum is that he called them by night and by day, in secret; then he called them aloud; then he called them both in secret and openly. This is how the one who enjoins good (al-amir bil-ma'ruf, one who commands what is right) acts: he begins with the easier, then the harder, and then the harder still. So he began with counsel in private, and when they did not accept, he repeated it with open proclamation, and when that had no effect, he combined private and open admonition together. The word "thumma" (then) indicates the distance between the states, because open proclaiming is harsher than private speaking, and combining the two is harsher than doing either one alone.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 71, verse 10:

﴿So I said: "Ask your Lord for forgiveness﴾, from shirk (association of partners with God), because istighfar (seeking forgiveness) is seeking forgiveness (maghfirah). If the one seeking forgiveness is a disbeliever, then it is from kufr (disbelief); and if he is a disobedient believer, then it is from sins,

﴿Indeed, He is ever Forgiving﴾, He has never ceased being Forgiving of the sins of those who turn back to Him.

﴿He sends down the sky﴾, meaning the rain,

﴿upon you in abundance﴾, meaning abundant in its pouring. The form *mif'āl* (مِفْعالٌ, an intensive adjective pattern), is one in which the masculine and the feminine are the same.

﴿And He will increase you in wealth and children﴾: He will add to you wealth and children.

﴿and will provide for you gardens﴾: orchards.

﴿and will provide for you rivers﴾: flowing, for your fields and your orchards. They loved wealth and children, so they were moved by this toward faith. It is also said: when they denied him after his prolonged repetition of the call, Allah withheld rain from them and rendered the wombs of their women barren for forty years, or seventy, so He promised them that if they believed, Allah would grant them abundance and remove from them what they were in.

It is related from ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with him) that he went out to seek rain (istisqa'), and he did nothing more than seek forgiveness (istighfar). He was asked: "We have not seen you seek rain." He said: "I have sought rain by the constellations of the sky through which rain is drawn down." ʿUmar likened istighfar to the truthful signs of the weather (anwa'), which never miss, and he recited the verses.

It is related from al-Hasan that a man complained to him of drought, and he said: "Seek forgiveness from Allah." Another complained to him of poverty, another of having few children, and another of little yield from his land, and he commanded all of them to seek forgiveness. Al-Rabi' said to him: "Men came to you complaining of closed doors, and you commanded them all to seek forgiveness." Then he recited the verses. (p-544)

ما لَكم لا تَرْجُونَ لِلَّهِ وقارًا (What is the matter with you that you do not hope for dignity from God?) means: لا تَخافُونَ لِلَّهِ عَظَمَةً (you do not fear the greatness of God). This is related by al-Akhfash (al-Akhfash, Abu al-Hasan), who said: "The word rajaʾ (hope), here, means fear (khawf), because with hope there is a part of fear and of despair." And al-Waqar (dignity) means greatness (al-ʿazama). Or the meaning is: لا تَأْمُلُونَ لَهُ تَوْقِيرًا (you do not expect from Him reverence), that is, تَعْظِيمًا (exaltation). The meaning is: ما لَكم لا تَكُونُونَ عَلى حالٍ تَأْمُلُونَ فِيها تَعْظِيمَ اللهِ إيّاكم في دارِ الثَوابِ (What is the matter with you that you are not in a state in which you hope for God's exalting of you in the abode of reward).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 71, verse 14:

﴿And He has created you in stages.﴾ It is in the position of a circumstantial clause (ḥāl), meaning: "What is wrong with you that you do not believe in Allah, while your state is this?" And this state is one that necessitates belief in Him, because He created you in stages (aṭwār), i.e., in successive times and repeated instances. He first created you as nutfah (a drop of fluid), then He created you as 'alaqah (a clinging clot), then He created you as mudghah (a lump of flesh), then He created you as bones and flesh. He first directed them to reflect upon themselves, because that is closer to them, and then to reflect upon the world and the wonders He arranged in it that point to the Creator, by His saying:

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 71, verse 15:

﴿Have you not seen how God created seven heavens in layers,﴾ one above another.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 71, verse 16:

﴿And He made the moon therein a light﴾, i.e., in the heavens, and it is in the lowest heaven (al-sama' al-dunya), because there is a connection between the heavens, in that they are layers (tibaq), so it is permissible to say, "therein is such-and-such," even if it is not in all of them, just as one says, "in the city is such-and-such," when it is in some of its quarters. It is related from Ibn 'Abbas and Ibn 'Umar, may Allah (Exalted) be pleased with them both, that the faces of the sun and the moon are turned toward the heavens, and their backs are toward the earth, so the light of the moon encompasses all the heavens, because they are subtle and do not block its light.

﴿And He made the sun a lamp (siraj)﴾, a lamp (misbah), by whose light the people of the world see, just as the people of a house see by the light of a lamp what they need to see. The light of the sun is stronger than the light of the moon. And they (the scholars) agreed that the sun is in the fourth heaven.

ِAnd God caused you to grow from the earth ﴿like plants﴾ — He brought you into being (anshaʾakum); the term "growing" (al-inbat) is used metaphorically for "bringing into being" (al-insha').

"Growth" (nabatan): you grew as a growth (fa-nabattum nabatan).

ثُمَّ يُعِيدُكُمْ فِيهَا﴾ — "Then He will return you into it" — after death.

﴿وَيُخْرِجُكُمْ﴾ — "and will bring you forth" — on the Day of Resurrection.

﴿إخْرَاجًا﴾ — "a [true] bringing forth." He emphasized it with the verbal noun (al-masdar), meaning: a bringing forth of such a kind [as is beyond doubt].

**Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 71, verse 19:**

(p-545) ﴿And Allah has made the earth a carpet for you﴾, spread out.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 71, verse 20:

﴿So that you may travel along them﴾, meaning: that you may move about on them as a man moves about on his carpet,

﴿roads﴾, meaning paths,

﴿wide﴾, meaning spacious, or ﴿varied﴾, meaning of different kinds.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 71, verse 21:

﴿Noah said: "My Lord, they have disobeyed me,"﴾ in what I commanded them of faith and seeking forgiveness.

﴿And they followed﴾ i.e., the lowly and the poor,

﴿one whose wealth and children increase him not, except in loss﴾ i.e., the leaders and the possessors of wealth and children. "Wa-waladuhu" (and his children), read by the Meccan and the Iraqi readers other than ʿĀṣim, is the plural of "walad" (child), like "asad" (lion) and "usd" (lions).

﴿except in loss﴾, in the Hereafter.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 71, verse 22:

﴿And they schemed﴾: it is coordinated (ma'tuf) with "lam yazidhu" (it did not increase him). The pronoun is in the plural, though it refers back to "man" (those who), because "man" carries the sense of plurality. The schemers are the leaders (al-ru'asa'). Their scheming (makruhum) is their deceit (ihtiyaluhum) regarding the religion, their plotting (kayduhum) against Nuh (Noah), their incitement (tahrish) of people to harm him, and their turning people away (sadduhum) from inclining towards him.

﴿a great scheme (makran kubbaran)﴾: 'azheeman (great). It is an intensified form (akbar) of "al-kibar", and it has been read with this form. It is also an intensified form (akbar) of "al-kabir".

**Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 71, verse 23:**

﴿And they said﴾, that is, the leaders, to their followers,

﴿"And they said: Do not abandon your gods"﴾, in general, that is, their worship,

﴿"Nor abandon Wadd"﴾, with a fatha or a damma on the waw, and the damma reading is that of Nafi'; they are two dialects. [Wadd is] an idol in the form of a man.

﴿"Nor Suwa'"﴾; it is in the form of a woman.

﴿"Nor Yaghuth"﴾; it is in the form of a lion.

﴿"And Ya'uq"﴾; it is in the form of a horse. Both of them are not declined (la yanṣarifan) because of definiteness (ta'rif) and the pattern of the verb (wazn al-fi'l), if they are Arabic; and because of definiteness and foreignness ('ujma), if they are non-Arabic.

﴿"And Nasr"﴾; it is in the form of a vulture. That is, these five idols in particular, and it seems they were the greatest of their idols and the most important to them; so they singled them out after the general mention. These idols passed from the people of Noah to the Arabs: Wadd belonged to the Kalb, Suwa' to Hamdan, Yaghuth to Madhhij, Ya'uq to Murad, and Nasr to Himyar. It is also said that they were names of righteous men whom people used to follow between Adam and Noah; when they died, they made their images so that this would be more conducive to them worshipping; then when time lengthened, Iblis said to them: "They used to worship them," so they worshipped them.

﴿وَقَدْ أضَلُّوا﴾ means: the idols (al-aṣnām), as in His saying: ﴿Indeed, they have led many of the people astray﴾ [Ibrahim: 36], (p-546) or the leaders.

﴿وَلا تَزِدِ الظالِمِينَ﴾ is coordinated (ʿaṭf) on "Lord, indeed they have disobeyed me," as part of the reported speech of Nuh (peace be upon him), after "he said," and after the waw that stands in for it. Its meaning is: "He said: 'My Lord, indeed they have disobeyed me,' and he said: 'Do not increase the wrongdoers...'" That is, he said these two statements, and both are in the accusative position, because they are the two objects of "he said."

﴿إلا ضَلالا﴾ means destruction (halakan), as in His saying: "And do not increase the wrongdoers except in ruin" (tabaran).

﴿Because of their sins﴾, "khatayahum" (their sins), is the reading of Abu 'Amr, meaning: their wrongdoings.

﴿They were drowned﴾ by the flood (al-tufan).

﴿And then they were made to enter a fire﴾, a great one. The placing of ﴿because of their sins﴾ first indicates that their drowning by the flood and their entry into the fires were only on account of their sins. This meaning is emphasised by the addition of "ma" (in "mimma"), and it is sufficient as a deterrent for one who commits sins. The disbelief of the people of Nuh was one of their sins, though it was the greatest of them. The "fa" in ﴿fa-udkhilu﴾ (then they were made to enter) indicates that they were punished by burning immediately after being drowned. This is therefore evidence for the affirmation of the punishment of the grave (adhab al-qabr).

﴿So they found for themselves no helpers besides Allah﴾, who would help them or protect them from the punishment of Allah.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 71, verse 26:

﴿And Noah said, "My Lord, do not leave upon the earth from among the disbelievers a single dweller."﴾ That is: anyone who moves about upon the earth. It is "fayyāl" (the intensive pattern), from "al-dawr" (turning, going about), and it is one of the nouns used in general negation.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 71, verse 27:

﴿Indeed, if You leave them﴾, and do not destroy them,

﴿they will mislead Your servants﴾, calling them to misguidance,

﴿and they will not beget except a wicked, ungrateful disbeliever﴾, except one who, when he reaches maturity, commits wickedness and disbelieves. He said this only because Allah (Exalted is He) informed him with His words: ﴿None will believe among your people except those who have already believed﴾ [Hud: 36].

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 71, verse 28:

﴿My Lord, forgive me and my parents﴾, and they were Muslims. The name of his father was Lamk, and the name of his mother was Shamkhaa. It is also said that they were Adam and Hawwa' (Eve). It was also read as "wa-liwaladayya" (and my sons), meaning Sam and Ham.

﴿And whoever enters my house﴾, my dwelling, or my mosque, or my ship,

﴿as a believer﴾, because he knew that whoever enters his house as a believer will not return to disbelief.

﴿As a believer, and for the believing men and believing women﴾, until the Day of Resurrection. He first singled out those who are connected to him, because they are more deserving and more entitled to his supplication; then he generalized to the believing men and believing women.

﴿And do not increase the wrongdoers﴾, that is: the disbelievers,

﴿except in ruin﴾, destruction, so they were destroyed.

Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, said: "Nuh (peace be upon him) made two supplications: one for the believers, for forgiveness, and the other against the disbelievers, for ruin. His supplication against the disbelievers was answered with ruin, so it was impossible that his supplication concerning the believers would not be answered."

Regarding their children at the time they were drowned, there is a difference of opinion. It is said: Allah rendered the wombs of their women barren forty years before the flood, so there were no children with them when they were drowned. It is also said: Allah knew their innocence, yet they were destroyed without punishment.
